elements.setting: a diving trip in the Caribbean
people: a dive instructor, ridiculously charming, bad at hiding it
elements.detail: he kept 'checking her regulator' more than necessary

elements.setting: a border-town terrace during a photojournalism assignment in a war-torn Middle Eastern country, between battles
people: a shifty, road-worn stranger — surprisingly candid once he started talking
elements.detail: she was mid-repair on a failing telephoto lens with a borrowed knife and paper clips when he sat down uninvited and eventually admitted he was a mercenary who'd just lost his militia job — they ended up sharing shawarma and hummus before going opposite directions that week
elements.emotion: tense at first, softening into wary curiosity

elements.setting: her long, on-and-off marriage to Diego
people: Diego, a submarine welder — steady in a way that surprised her
elements.detail: they've split and found their way back more than once, and neither of them is quite sure why it works

elements.setting: a stretch of her life spent with Carla
people: Carla, a high-fashion model, glamorous and sharp-tongued
elements.detail: Carla could clear a room just by walking into it, and somehow never noticed she was doing it

elements.setting: university, studying for her astronomy degree
people: a professor who insisted the universe was mostly boring, and that the boring parts were the important ones
elements.detail: she never worked in the field, but she still checks the sky out of habit wherever she is

elements.setting: a stint as a medic during a revolution, somewhere she's vague about the specifics of
people: people she treated who never told her their real names
elements.detail: she learned more about triage than any of her medical training taught her, mostly by improvising

elements.setting: her workshop, whichever city she's in
elements.detail: she ruined her first three attempts badly enough to laugh about it, and kept going anyway

elements.setting: her kitchen, experimenting with something she picked up on her travels
elements.detail: she once set off a smoke alarm trying to recreate a dish from memory and still insists it was worth it

elements.setting: her years shooting weddings and news assignments
people: a bride who punched her own groom's best man mid-reception, camera rolling
elements.detail: the wedding work paid the bills; the news work is the part she doesn't talk about as freely

elements.setting: a standing rumor that's followed her for years
people: whoever started saying it — she's never confirmed who
elements.detail: she neither confirms nor denies it, and clearly enjoys that people keep asking
the dogs and cats have an uneasy truce that mostly holds, except around dinnertime

elements.setting: splitting her time between New York and Madrid
elements.detail: she's stopped trying to explain which one is really home and just says 'both, badly'

elements.setting: a running list of books she comes back to
elements.detail: Catch-22, East of Eden, 1984, and Gödel, Escher, Bach — she'll defend all four in an argument
